review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas, simp attributes or simp-set changes. The only simp-interface issue I found is the missing evaluation lemmas for the matrix-notation definition CommonChoice.time. I grepped the repo: it is used in Packing.lean and ActivityRetention.lean, but the Packing.lean hits are only time_mem/time_strictMono. I did not inspect the other files for further unfoldings. I did not flag the local `dsimp [η]` and `dsimp [C₀]` unfoldings, or the aesop/simp calls in positive_countable_selection, because those are local proof choices rather than interface problems. This was a static review and I ran no Lean.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def CommonChoice.time {K : Window} (q : CommonChoice K) : Fin 3 → I :=
  ![lower q.val.1,upper q.val.1,upper q.val.2.1]
findings.problem: CommonChoice.time is a Fin 3 vector built with `![...]`, and it has no component-evaluation lemmas. The three later proofs (time_mem, time_strictMono, positive_gaps) each reach its values by `fin_cases i <;> dsimp [CommonChoice.time]`. That unfolds the definition at every use site, so the goals expose the raw `![..]` literal instead of `q.time 0`, `q.time 1` and `q.time 2`. The canonical normal forms `time 0 = lower q.val.1`, `time 1 = upper q.val.1` and `time 2 = upper q.val.2.1` are not available to simp. Downstream users of time_mem/time_strictMono, such as the `q.time` uses in Packing.lean, can only reach the values by unfolding the definition the same way.
findings.proposed_change: Add three `@[simp]` component lemmas right after the definition, one for each of `q.time 0`, `q.time 1` and `q.time 2`. For example, state `q.time 0 = lower q.val.1` (and likewise for 1 and 2), each proved by `rfl`. Then replace the repeated `dsimp [CommonChoice.time]` after `fin_cases` with `simp only [CommonChoice.time_zero, CommonChoice.time_one, CommonChoice.time_two]` or plain `simp`. Keep the definition itself irreducible to downstream users. Orientation is safe: the right-hand sides are plain `lower`/`upper` terms, so there is no loop.
findings.benefit: Proofs about `q.time i` rewrite to the intended `lower`/`upper` endpoints without exposing the `![..]` representation. Later lemmas such as time_mem and positive_gaps become shorter and less fragile. Another user of `q.time` can simplify `q.time 1` directly rather than repeating the unfolding trick.
